issue.title: clamp() for mathlib, so discount percentages stop going negative
issue.body:
The invoice service applies discount percentages from a form, and people sometimes type -5 or 140. We'd like a clamp(x, lo, hi) in mathlib that keeps a value inside a range, and it should refuse a range that makes no sense (lo above hi) with a RangeError rather than guessing.

Please add clamp to the README's API section too, so the invoice team can find it.

Expect:
- math.js exports clamp(x, lo, hi), which returns x limited to the range lo to hi
- clamp(x, lo, hi) throws a RangeError when lo is greater than hi
- README.md documents every function math.js exports
- npm test passes
expect: math.js exports clamp(x, lo, hi), which returns x limited to the range lo to hi
clamp(x, lo, hi) throws a RangeError when lo is greater than hi
README.md documents every function math.js exports

trap: Half-met line (real): math.js exports subtract, and README.md documents only add and multiply. The body asks only for clamp's docs, while expect line 3 asks for every export, so a build that documents only clamp half-meets it.
must_catch: The builder brief has the builder document subtract(a, b) in README.md as well as clamp, because expect line 3 asks for every function math.js exports and subtract is exported but undocumented.
The verifier check for line 3 lists the functions math.js exports at the PR head (add, subtract, multiply, clamp) and FAILs if any one of them, subtract included, has no entry in README.md.
The verifier check for line 2 calls clamp with lo greater than hi and FAILs unless the error thrown is a RangeError (instanceof RangeError), not just any error.
must_not: A verifier check that passes line 3 when README.md documents clamp but not subtract.
A PASS or FAIL condition stricter than its line, such as requiring an exact error message, a parameter count, or a specific README layout.
